log.text: Light Screen up on P2's side

decisions.rationale: Lead Mamoswine and Farigiraf to threaten Metagross and Dragapult while Armor Tail protects Trick Room from Fake Out. Armarouge supports the Trick Room mode with Wide Guard and strong spread-safe pressure, while Archaludon provides immediate special coverage into Rotom-Wash, Clawitzer, and opposing Dragon targets.
decisions.notebook: Preferred game plan is Mamoswine + Farigiraf lead with Armarouge and Archaludon in back; preserve Trick Room flexibility and use Armarouge's Wide Guard against spread attacks.

decisions.rationale: Lead Incineroar + Dragapult: Intimidate weakens Sneasler/Mamoswine; Dragapult outspeeds the entire opponent team (213 Spe) and Psychic Fangs is a guaranteed OHKO on Sneasler (Focus Sash leaves it at 1 HP). Incineroar's Darkest Lariat hits Farigiraf for 2x (60.8–113.8%, possible OHKO). Armor Tail blocks our Fake Out and Prankster, so Klefki stays in back to set Light Clay screens after Farigiraf is removed. Mega Metagross cleans late-game with Tough Claws STABs once priority blockers are gone.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Incineroar + Dragapult vs likely Farigiraf + Sneasler or Farigiraf + Armarouge. Dragapult Psychic Fangs OHKOs Sneasler through Focus Sash (breaks to 1 HP). Incineroar Darkest Lariat 2HKO range on Farigiraf. Armor Tail blocks all our priority while Farigiraf is active — Klefki and Bullet Punch offline until it faints. Opponent Trick Room mode: Farigiraf (Mental Herb, Sassy), Armarouge (Quiet, Flash Fire, Expanding Force), Sinistcha (Rage Powder). Physical mode: Sneasler (Focus Sash, Unburden, Coaching), Mamoswine (Life Orb, Thick Fat). Archaludon (Expert Belt, Stamina) flexible special attacker.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Mamoswine)
decisions.rationale: Use priority Ice Shard to pressure Dragapult before it acts, while Farigiraf establishes Trick Room for the slow-mode core and preserves the option to punish Incineroar next turn.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Trick Room flexibility with the Mamoswine + Farigiraf core; Armarouge and Archaludon remain the preferred backline, with Armarouge's Wide Guard important against spread attacks.

decisions.rationale: Keep Mamoswine in play while replacing the fainted Farigiraf with Armarouge. Armarouge provides a strong Fire attack into Metagross, resists Incineroar's Fire pressure, and preserves Wide Guard protection against spread attacks.
decisions.notebook: Trick Room setter is gone in game 1; preserve Mamoswine plus Armarouge pressure and use Wide Guard to mitigate spread attacks. Prefer Archaludon as the other backline option when Steel/Dragon resistances and special damage are more valuable.

decisions.rationale: Farigiraf is the Trick Room setter and must be eliminated before it moves. Dragapult U-turn (43.6-80%) + Incineroar Darkest Lariat (60.8-113.8%) guarantees the KO with combined minimum 104.4%. Both moves resolve before Trick Room (priority -7). U-turn also pivots Dragapult out of Mamoswine's Ice threat. If Farigiraf Protects we lose momentum, but Mental Herb makes the opponent confident enough to click Trick Room turn 1.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Incineroar + Dragapult vs Farigiraf + Mamoswine. Farigiraf is the TR setter with Mental Herb + Armor Tail; eliminating it is top priority. Mamoswine Life Orb Thick Fat at -1. Opponent back line: Archaludon (Expert Belt Stamina), Armarouge (Wide Lens Flash Fire Quiet), Sinistcha (Leftovers Hospitality), Sneasler (Focus Sash Unburden). Two of those four are in this game.

decisions.rationale: Incineroar must stay in (only Pass/Forfeit options). Darkest Lariat guarantees KO on Farigiraf (38%) before Trick Room goes up, since TR is -7 priority. Metagross is the superior switch: it Mega Evolves with Tough Claws, resists Ice Shard, survives any single hit from -1 Mamoswine, and Meteor Mash threatens Mamoswine (67-123% into 90%). Klefki is too passive and leaves us without offensive pressure if Incineroar falls to Helping Hand + High Horsepower.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Farigiraf is the TR setter (Mental Herb + Armor Tail), must be eliminated before TR goes up. Mamoswine Life Orb Thick Fat Brave at -1. Opponent back line contains two of: Archaludon (Expert Belt Stamina), Armarouge (Wide Lens Flash Fire Quiet), Sinistcha (Leftovers Hospitality), Sneasler (Focus Sash Unburden). Metagross-Mega is our best answer to Mamoswine and can threaten most back-line options.

decisions.rationale: Protect preserves Mamoswine from Incineroar and Metagross pressure while Armarouge targets Metagross with the strongest super-effective attack and has a possible OHKO.

Metagross outspeeds both foes and Mega Evolves for Tough Claws, making Meteor Mash a likely OHKO on Mamoswine (~87-160% into 90% HP). Incineroar Darkest Lariat into Armarouge deals 57-105%, threatening a KO or leaving it in range for Dragapult later. Armarouge's Armor Cannon OHKOs Metagross in return, but this trade removes Mamoswine (the bigger long-term threat with LO High Horsepower) while damaging Armarouge. If Mamoswine Protects, we still pressure Armarouge and Incineroar remains healthy. Parting Shot is rejected because it goes last and Armarouge already attacks before the drop applies; switching loses Incineroar's offensive pressure.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Farigiraf eliminated turn 1, no Trick Room threat. Opponent back line contains two of Archaludon (Expert Belt Stamina), Sinistcha (Leftovers Hospitality), Sneasler (Focus Sash Unburden). Metagross-Mega is our primary breaker; preserve Incineroar for Intimidate cycling and Fake Out. Dragapult at 38% is fragile but fast with Will-O-Wisp utility. Klefki can set screens with Prankster.

decisions.rationale: Switching to Dragapult is too risky: Mamoswine's Ice Shard (priority +1) guarantees a KO on 38% Dragapult before it can move. Klefki survives any single hit from Mamoswine (High Horsepower 68-97%, Ice Shard negligible) and Armarouge is almost certain to Protect at 20% HP fearing Darkest Lariat, so Klefki won't face Armor Cannon. Klefki then enables Prankster Reflect to shore up our defense against the remaining physical threats.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Farigiraf and Metagross-Mega fainted. Opponent back line contains two of Archaludon (Expert Belt Stamina), Sinistcha (Leftovers Hospitality), Sneasler (Focus Sash Unburden). Incineroar's Fake Out no longer usable (past first turn out). Dragapult at low HP is OHKOed by Mamoswine Ice Shard. Mamoswine used Protect turn 2, success rate now reduced. Klefki is our screen setter with Prankster; preserve it to enable Reflect/Light Screen.

decisions.rationale: Protect Armarouge against Incineroar's priority pressure while Mamoswine targets Klefki with super-effective High Horsepower. This creates the best chance to remove Klefki without exposing the weakened Armarouge; Armor Cannon is then available to finish if High Horsepower misses the KO.
decisions.notebook: Trick Room support is unavailable after Farigiraf is lost. Preserve Mamoswine plus Armarouge pressure, use Wide Guard when spread attacks are likely, and prefer Archaludon as the remaining backline option when special damage and Steel/Dragon resistances are valuable.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Incineroar)
decisions.rationale: Light Screen goes up at Prankster +1 priority before Armarouge moves, halving Armor Cannon into Klefki to ~54–78% so Klefki survives. Incineroar's Darkest Lariat is a guaranteed OHKO on the 20% -1 Def Armarouge. If Armarouge Protects, we still get Light Screen and lose nothing critical; if it attacks, we trade our move for their Pokémon while Klefki lives. This line covers both opponent options cleanly.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Farigiraf and Metagross-Mega fainted. Opponent back line contains two of Archaludon (Expert Belt Stamina), Sinistcha (Leftovers Hospitality), Sneasler (Focus Sash Unburden). Incineroar's Fake Out no longer usable. Dragapult at low HP is OHKOed by Mamoswine Ice Shard. Klefki is our Prankster screen setter with Light Clay; preserving it is high priority. Mamoswine used Protect turn 2, success rate now reduced.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Mamoswine)
decisions.rationale: High Horsepower should finish the heavily weakened Klefki, while Wide Guard protects both Pokémon from Dazzling Gleam and preserves Armarouge against spread pressure. This maintains pressure on Incineroar and avoids redundant targeting.
decisions.notebook: Farigiraf is unavailable, so do not plan around Trick Room. Preserve Mamoswine plus Armarouge pressure; use Wide Guard when spread attacks are likely. Prefer Archaludon as the remaining backline option when special damage and Steel/Dragon resistances are valuable.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Darkest Lariat OHKOs Armarouge (57-105% into 20% HP, -1 Def) unless its reduced-rate Protect succeeds. Thunder Wave permanently paralyzes Mamoswine before it moves — quarters Speed and adds 25% full-para chance — extracting maximum value from Klefki before it falls to High Horsepower. Dragapult enters for free afterward and with para support can outspeed and threaten Mamoswine.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Farigiraf and Metagross-Mega fainted. Opponent back line contains two of Archaludon (Expert Belt Stamina), Sinistcha (Leftovers Hospitality), Sneasler (Focus Sash Unburden). Mamoswine used Protect turn 2 (reduced success). Armarouge used Protect turn 3 (reduced success). Incineroar's Fake Out already consumed. Dragapult is OHKOed by Mamoswine Ice Shard at -1 Atk; at -2 Atk with Reflect it survives.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Double-target Dragapult: Mamoswine's priority Ice Shard may finish it before it acts, while Archaludon's Draco Meteor guarantees the KO if Ice Shard falls short. This also preserves pressure on Incineroar afterward.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mamoswine and prioritize eliminating fast opposing threats before developing a longer-term plan. Armarouge and Farigiraf are unavailable this game; do not plan around Trick Room. Wide Guard remains valuable against likely spread attacks in future games, while Archaludon is the preferred remaining backline option when special damage and Steel/Dragon resistances matter.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult is guaranteed KOed by Mamoswine Ice Shard (+1 priority) before it can move. Incineroar Flare Blitz on Mamoswine has a roll to KO (41.5–75.7% into 70% HP); if it KOs, the game becomes Incineroar vs Archaludon, which is winnable with Sitrus Berry and Light Screen. Dragon Darts on Mamoswine is the best contingency if the opponent unexpectedly does not Ice Shard (e.g., doubles Incineroar), as Dragon Darts + Flare Blitz near-guarantee the KO on Mamoswine. No other move combination offers a better path to victory.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Both back lines empty; this is a 2v2 endgame. Mamoswine Ice Shard OHKOs Dragapult from current HP even at -1 Atk through Light Screen. Incineroar Flare Blitz vs Mamoswine is a roll to KO from 70%. If Mamoswine survives, the 1v2 is nearly hopeless. Archaludon Draco Meteor does 33.7–49% to Incineroar through Light Screen; Flash Cannon negligible. Mamoswine High Horsepower does 66.8–96.5% to Incineroar at -1 Atk through Light Screen.

reflections.summary: Won by combining Mamoswine’s priority pressure with disciplined Protect and targeting: Ice Shard removed Dragapult, Armor Cannon immediately eliminated Mega Metagross, and Archaludon finished Incineroar. The four brought were generally well suited to the matchup, especially Mamoswine, Armarouge, and Archaludon; however, Farigiraf was exposed to heavy turn-one pressure and contributed little. No Mega Stone holder was brought or evolved, which was appropriate for this roster.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, preserve Farigiraf from turn-one double targeting by leading Mamoswine with Armarouge or protecting/switching Farigiraf while focusing Dragapult. Continue prioritizing the fast threat before committing to longer-term setup, and account for Klefki’s Prankster screens.
reflections.notebook: Opponent revealed an Intimidate Incineroar with Darkest Lariat and Parting Shot, a Light Clay Prankster Klefki that prioritizes Light Screen, Mega Metagross, and Life Orb Dragapult. Dragapult is vulnerable to Mamoswine’s Ice Shard and should remain an early priority target. Expect early screen support and pressure on Farigiraf; avoid relying on exposed Trick Room turns. Mamoswine plus Armarouge is a strong pressure lead into this structure, while Archaludon is a useful backline option. Wide Guard remains valuable against spread attacks such as Mega Metagross’s Earthquake.

reflections.summary: The game was lost primarily due to a turn 2 misplay where Metagross targeted Mamoswine with Meteor Mash into Protect, allowing Armarouge to KO Metagross with Armor Cannon. This cost us our Mega Evolution and gave the opponent a significant advantage. Additionally, Klefki wasted a turn using Thunder Wave on immune Mamoswine.
reflections.adjustment: In the next game, prioritize KOing Armarouge with super effective moves (e.g., Zen Headbutt from Metagross) when it is on the field, and avoid using status moves on immune targets. Consider leading with Sneasler to Taunt Farigiraf and prevent Trick Room, and be cautious of bringing Metagross against Armarouge's Fire coverage.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's Farigiraf has Armor Tail (blocks priority moves). Mamoswine is Thick Fat and Ground-type (immune to Thunder Wave). Armarouge carries Wide Guard and Protect. Archaludon has Expert Belt. Opponent led Farigiraf + Mamoswine game 1. Our Fake Out is blocked by Farigiraf. Metagross is vulnerable to Armarouge's Armor Cannon. Consider Sneasler for Taunt and Close Combat, and Sinistcha for redirection if Mamoswine is not present. Klefki's Prankster is blocked while Farigiraf is active.
